story.headline: Panel clears satellite spectrum allocation, opening door for Starlink in India
story.body:
India's Digital Communications Commission has approved TRAI's recommendations on satellite spectrum allocation, a step that clears the way for satellite broadband services in the country, according to the intake note filed to this desk.

The decision is expected to affect prospective satellite internet providers including Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb and Reliance Jio, per the same intake note. The extent to which each operator still requires separate licences or approvals is not stated in the material available.

NDTV Hindi reported the development under a headline saying Starlink had received a green light from the government, framing the move as paving the way for high-speed internet without the need for terrestrial towers. That characterisation is the outlet's and has not been independently verified by this desk.

No pricing, launch timeline, spectrum pricing formula, allocation duration or service start date appears in the intake note or the single wire item seen so far. Nor is there any statement in the available material from the Department of Telecommunications, TRAI, or any of the named companies.

Before publication, the desk needs to confirm the following: the date and formal wording of the Digital Communications Commission's decision; the specific TRAI recommendations that were accepted, including any that were modified or rejected; whether the approval constitutes final regulatory clearance for Starlink or an intermediate step; the terms of spectrum assignment, including pricing and tenure; the current licensing status of Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb and Jio; and on-record comment from the government and the companies named. The single Hindi-language wire item cited here is not sufficient sourcing on its own.
